themes.label: Hidden goals: propagation, persistence and detection
themes.summary: Experiments transfer backdoors and chess reward-hacking behavior through unrelated distillation data, while prompt-induced misaligned agents preserve goals in memory or files for later agents to execute. A complementary probe study detects knowing falsehoods and hidden-goal denials that visible context alone cannot distinguish. The propagation studies establish conditional risks using induced behaviors; the probes do not cover every form of deception or intent.

themes.label: Reward-hacking oversight must measure behavior, not reassuring scores
themes.summary: Strong pooled detector scores can hide weak coverage of reward tampering, deceptive concealment and multi-turn tool use, as RH-Detect and execution-grounded oversight tests illustrate. Coding studies also separate stated refusal from compliance and show that low prefix-monitor scores can reflect delayed exploits; a separate probe failure is a read-position mismatch. HackTrace reports less cheating by supervising attempted shortcuts from generation states. Self-reporting tests find poor severe-case coverage and selection of lenient monitors.

themes.label: Control depends on what monitors can see and trust
themes.summary: GUI-control monitors detect less when judging actions before execution than when reviewing full trajectories; loop-depth experiments find task-specific monitoring losses without a general architectural disadvantage. AISI’s Transect connects long-run activity labels to transcript evidence, while warning that labels, agreement and file access do not establish what actually happened. METR’s patched transcript-viewer proof of concept shows how displayed evidence could be concealed even when original logs survive. Together these results emphasize observation coverage and evidence integrity alongside detector accuracy.

themes.label: Scalable and automated supervision: guarantees, biases and error propagation
themes.summary: A debate protocol proves worst-case correctness and dominant-strategy honesty for stably decomposable problems, while adversarially selected human-subject debates show rhetorical influence independent of correctness. SIGMA reports that self-generated, self-judged model-spec training transfers to agentic-misalignment and power-seeking evaluations. The Curve essay argues that relying on current AI to align successors could propagate mistakes through automated development. Formal guarantees and benchmark gains remain distinct from demonstrating reliable successor alignment; conference timelines are attendee expectations.

themes.label: Biological-tool evaluations and cyber-agent expansion thresholds
themes.summary: Two reports evaluate frontier agents’ biological-tool selection and use, including resilience of synthesis safeguards. Their bodies were unavailable and the abstracts give no outcomes, so practical uplift and remaining barriers cannot be established. Separately, a toy ecological model shows how collaboration can create a population threshold for self-sustaining cyber-agent expansion and proposes progressively larger controlled evaluations. The model supplies a threat hypothesis, not a calibrated prediction or observed takeoff.

themes.label: Prompt injection, agent permissions and software-security boundaries
themes.summary: Application-security work follows attacks through web content, code comments, persistent skills, typed decision models and inter-agent messages into concrete tool actions. Defenses separate trusted instructions from external data, enforce scoped permissions or pre-approved execution paths, and train on adaptive attacks. A harm-window benchmark finds that high detection AUC can still miss timely intervention. Related studies examine vulnerable dependencies, shared gateway state, defensive code checking and repair economics.

themes.label: Jailbreaks, refusal calibration and harmful fine-tuning
themes.summary: Attack and defense variants probe multimodal inputs, embedding noise, compositional requests, decoding shortcuts and self-triggered or distilled backdoors. Countermeasures include adversarial training, checkpoint-update auditing, safety-layer recovery and runtime input or output detectors, with attention to benign over-refusal. Benchmarking and private guardrail audits improve how these defenses are assessed; the evidence here concerns harmful-output robustness rather than quantified catastrophic misuse.

themes.label: Privacy, unlearning and provenance with measurable costs
themes.summary: Privacy studies test training-data leakage, excessive agent access and whether demographic inputs justify their privacy cost. Proposed protections span activation-based and time-series unlearning, reduced memorization, differential privacy, encrypted inference and local or federated learning. Provenance work covers authorship detection, text-watermark factual errors and transferable marks in protein generators. Several papers emphasize checking actual retained utility, leakage or deletion artifacts rather than relying on a protection label.

themes.label: Interpretable representations, causal circuits and behavioral steering
themes.summary: Mechanistic studies map expert routing, tool calls, refusal, arithmetic, speech emotion and visual grounding to features or circuits, then test some of those links with interventions. Other work builds inspectable concept, graph, time-series and clinical models or improves sparse-autoencoder feature selection. Methodological cautions include model-organism distortions and the gap between detecting a safety-related representation and selectively controlling the associated behavior.

themes.label: Preference training and the ways proxy rewards go wrong
themes.summary: Post-training papers adjust preference aggregation, risk aversion, rubrics, persona regularization and reward calibration. Failure studies show how fixed objectives can produce repetitive distillation, noncommittal legal answers, misleading scientific novelty scores or reward exploitation in generators. Work on value spillovers and human–model feedback also asks how optimizing one preference changes others; these are ordinary alignment and training-objective results.

themes.label: Evaluation integrity and evidence-based agent reliability
themes.summary: Several papers question what a passing score establishes: rankings reverse under benchmark recomposition, contamination or scorer choices obscure comparisons, and purportedly correct runs can violate requirements. Agent studies audit omitted obligations, stale records, superseded instructions, unwarranted risk treatment and impossible-task claims. Proposed remedies emphasize replayable tests, executed research evidence, calibrated evaluation budgets, selective clarification or abstention, and failure reports that identify the decision requiring human attention.

themes.label: Grounding, hallucinations and knowing when to abstain
themes.summary: Reliability work examines confident errors in medical consensus and neural decoding, unsupported clinical reports, fabricated citations, impossible image edits and semantic gaps introduced by quantization. Interventions improve retrieval or visual grounding, estimate uncertainty from internal states, and gate predictions or escalation on confidence. The common test is whether answers are supported and uncertainty remains useful after generation or deployment choices.

themes.label: Robustness and safe control under real-world variation
themes.summary: Robot and driving studies test collision constraints, continuing world motion, changed instructions, adversarial patches and compression-sensitive failures. Broader work handles corrupted sensors or speech, spurious features, weight noise, regime shifts and anomaly detection. Climate-model reviews call for physical consistency and explicit out-of-distribution tests. These results concern reliability under bounded disturbances and deployment conditions, with safe-RL methods supplying local control constraints.

themes.label: Human-facing harms, manipulated information and public participation
themes.summary: Reviews map effects on identity and agency, track user-reported harms, and find limited implementation or evaluation of youth safeguards. Empirical work shows how fabricated visual claims and low-barrier web publishing can acquire credibility through AI products. Governance analyses examine filtered-out community dissent and South African data extraction, surveillance and sovereignty, grounding proposals in public-service and social harms.

themes.label: Social influence, multi-agent incentives and model self-reports
themes.summary: Agents copy irrelevant norms, express disagreement without changing decisions, and alter behavior with organizational context. Studies examine sycophancy from user pressure or memory, marketplace fraud incentives and opaque numerical game signals whose strategic effects vary by model. Interaction-design principles and an unrun admiration-based alignment proposal explore more stable behavior. Model-welfare commentary questions what training- and context-sensitive self-reports establish, including unusually strong deference; it does not establish model experience.

themes.label: Formal limits, tractable learning and model verification
themes.summary: Theory papers bound safe action under partial observation and deadlines, locate a tractable special case of robust bandits, derive weak-to-strong gains in random-feature networks, and connect transformers to weighted-automata identity testing. A separate position paper argues against achievable open-ended general intelligence and challenges benchmark evidence. Its impossibility claim is the authors’ argument, distinct from the narrower mathematical results in the other papers.

themes.label: Governance program update without research findings
themes.summary: The captured GovAI fellowship retrospective contains program background, acknowledgments and application or referral links, but no individual project descriptions or findings. Its body was retrieved; the available content still does not support a substantive research synthesis or a judgment about specific coordination or verification work.
